label: Confirmed Deaths
contestNote: Toll held flat at 111 for six days (27 Aug–2 Sep) before jumping sharply to 127 on 3 September — the largest single-update rise since late August. BNPB attributes the jump to continued identification/verification work in outlying villages and additional indirect-impact deaths rather than a new incident, but has not published a detailed breakdown explaining the size of the jump. Regency split: Manggarai 51, East Manggarai 40, Nagekeo 20, Sikka 6, Ngada 6, Ende 3, West Manggarai 1.

label: Injured
contestNote: BNPB's 3 September 09:00 WIB tally of 1,712 is up from 1,631 (30 Aug); the injured count has swung both up and down across reporting days as regency-level tallies are reconciled and some cases are discharged or reclassified.

label: Displaced / Sheltering
contestNote: Displacement fell to 166,829 on the 3 September 09:00 WIB count, continuing the decline from a 188,161 peak on 30 August as more families return home or move into more permanent shelter — the clearest sustained downward trend since the quake.

label: Homes Damaged
contestNote: A provincial BPBD NTT tally as of 2 September put homes damaged at 99,214 (26,092 severe, 22,525 moderate, 50,597 light) — higher than BNPB's own 95,567 national figure from 30 August. The same provincial count found 2,310 education units, 664 government offices, 600 houses of worship, 654 health facilities, 6,840 other public facilities and 36 water systems damaged, a broader facility breakdown than BNPB has published nationally. Figures remain preliminary pending reconciliation between provincial and national counts.
delta: +3,647 since 30 Aug (BPBD NTT vs BNPB baseline)

label: Aftershocks Recorded
deltaNote: M0.6–M6.2 range; 10,232 by 31 August, 10,937 by 1 September, and 11,630 by 3 September 05:00 WIB (168 felt by residents, up from 164). BMKG says the decay curve continues showing a clearer declining pattern, with activity still expected to continue another 3-4 weeks from the mainshock — pointing toward late September for stabilization. A M4.3 aftershock 47km north of Ruteng was felt (MMI II) on the morning of 4 September with no reported damage.

label: Presidential Visit Status
deltaNote: Twice-postponed visit finally took place on Day 11 (26 Aug); Prabowo distributed Rp200 billion in aid at a Nagekeo Regency command post.

label: Personnel Deployed
delta: 5,832 TNI + 238 Polri + 903 volunteers as of 22-23 Aug (up from 3,500+ TNI/Polri on 17 Aug)

label: State of Emergency
deltaNote: Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena extended the province-wide emergency response status by 14 days beyond its original 28 August expiry, citing forecast aftershock activity continuing another 2-3 weeks; Nagekeo Regency received a separate 3-month extension.

label: Mainshock Magnitude
contestNote: GFZ Potsdam measured Mw 7.61 at 25 km depth vs. USGS/BMKG's M7.7 at 10 km; BMKG's own first report was M7.0 before revising upward.

label: Schools Damaged
contestNote: BPBD NTT's provincial tally as of 2 September counted 2,310 education units damaged, higher than Kemendikdasmen's own 1,918-unit assessment from 31 August (665 schools severely damaged, ~141,207 students affected, only 37 back to in-person classes and 295 on distance learning). A companion Kemendikdasmen breakdown put severely damaged classrooms at 6,927, with 418 laboratories, 1,928 toilets and 370 teacher residences also damaged, and 48,164 school-community members displaced; 785 schools had requested emergency classroom units (2,908 needed), only 89 emergency tents were installed as of 30 August, and 1,221 schools remained halted from in-person learning. Provincial and ministry counts have not yet been reconciled.

label: Aid Distributed (Cumulative)
deltaNote: Delivered via TNI AU airlift (565t + a further 21t on 30 Aug), the Ready-to-Use Fund (1,065t), sea transport (179t) and overland trucking (145t); reaching distribution hubs in Maumere and Labuan Bajo. Separately, the Air Force said its Halim Perdanakusuma-coordinated relief airlift — 729 tons of food and clothing via C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft — was winding down after a 15-day operation.
